question: Does a learned router beat the deterministic incumbent on a properly held-out mix that the incumbent does NOT saturate?

candidate.description: M281's closed-form ridge over frozen mean-pooled BERT features, fit UNCHANGED

train.note: the M281 training set exactly (cell-4 templates/generators)

incumbent.description: cosine nearest-centroid embedding router, the sealed cell-4 rule

arithmetic_paraphrase.note: NEW templates only — disjoint from the cell-4 template set the candidate trains on

logic_paraphrase.note: NEW question forms — disjoint from the cell-4 form

confounder.note: cross-cue: task = logic, surface = arithmetic (half true, half false)

digit_arithmetic.note: digit-form arithmetic — a surface neither the centroids nor the candidate trained on

sentiment.note: disjoint from the candidate's training rows [3000, 3300) and from the sealed cell-4 rows [2500, 2800)

gates.g1_premise: incumbent misroutes > 0 on this mix, measured FIRST (a void run reads no candidate number)
gates.g2_heldout: test templates/forms disjoint from the candidate's training set; sentiment rows disjoint
gates.g3_admission: strictly fewer misroutes than the incumbent, or equal misroutes with strictly higher routed accuracy measured under the candidate's own routes; a tie is not admission
